subject.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `question.*`, `operator.questions`, and the Plugin SDK question resolver as a permanent provider-neutral core contract now, rather than keeping structured human input limited to provider-specific bridges?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally broader than a bug fix: it creates a new durable Gateway authorization, RPC, event, Plugin SDK, channel, and native-client surface. The code can be mechanically completed, but whether this is the desired long-term core boundary requires maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the provider-neutral contract
options.body: Accept the core direction after the native operator-scope gap is fixed and final-head web/channel proof confirms the complete authorization and delivery path.

options.title: Keep questions provider-specific
options.body: Decline the new core RPC/SDK surface and retain structured question handling only in existing provider bridges such as the Codex integration.

options.title: Narrow the scope first
options.body: Require a smaller initial core seam with channel and native-client expansion deferred to follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the provider-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Accept the core direction after the native operator-scope gap is fixed and final-head web/channel proof confirms the complete authorization and delivery path.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns both the merged predecessor and the current cross-layer proposal, making them the best available routing candidate for the intended core boundary.
